hook.text: An MCC is a special type of MCS—nearly circular on satellite, with a cold cloud top spanning 100,000 km² or more.

buildup.text: MCCs form in the evening, peak around midnight, and dissipate by morning—a predictable nocturnal cycle.

discovery.text: Their massive anvils can cover an entire state—making them easily identifiable in infrared satellite imagery.

twist.text: MCCs are among the most efficient rain producers on Earth—critical for agriculture across the Great Plains.

climax.text: Despite their importance, MCCs are hard to forecast—their initiation depends on subtle interactions aloft.

punchline.text: A storm the size of a state—visible only from space.
